articles.title: What's behind the AI industry’s latest warnings of doom? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The AI industry seems to be having its loudest debate yet about whether its technology poses an existential threat to humanity.
The current discussion began after AI researcher Jacob Coxon said that he’s resigned from Anthropic because he’s worried that the leading AI companies are “gambling with our lives.” Then Anthropic’s alignment lead chimed in with a post declaring, “We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!” adding that he personally thinks the chance is “>10% within the next decade.”
On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed the latest apocalyptic warnings. I tried to articulate why I’m skeptical of many AI doomer narratives, while Kirsten asked if this was “just a weird way of flexing to show how far advanced their company’s AI model is,” particularly as these companies prepare to go public.
And Sean wondered how these concerns might show up in Anthropic’s S-1 filing for its IPO: “Are there junior lawyers right now who are going through and having to rewrite that entire section of the S-1 filing to say, ‘It’s a officially Anthropic’s position that there’s a more than 10% chance that we could develop something that would eradicate all of humanity and that would be materially bad for our business’?”
Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity. (Note: We recorded this episode before Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published his plan for more cautious AI development.)
Sean: I’m hard-pressed to think of something that blew up so fast. Not only did this warning shot come out from this young researcher who has also worked at OpenAI, but also was immediately shared on X by the alignment lead at Anthropic — who, in what might go down as one of the best misplaced exclamation marks ever, shared Coxon’s post and and thread and said, “We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!” Exclamation mark!
What a weird vibe. That was just a ton of accelerant on an already fraught post or series of posts. Coming after the Hugging Face hack from OpenAI’s internal model, plus just the increased capabilities we’ve seen with the latest models released by Anthropic and and now OpenAI with with Astra a few weeks ago, I think this was just perfectly timed to be a powder keg type of thing for this young researcher to say.
Anthony: Just to disagree with you, I do think that if you believe that AI could destroy all humanity, that does deserve an exclamation point. I would argue that that is a perfectly well-used exclamation point!
My issue with that tweet was more the “we.” Who is the “we” here? To what extent can we talk about sort of the AI community or AI research community as a monolith? And the greater than 10% chance — that’s just a made-up number, that doesn’t mean anything. Sometimes [there is] this habit in both the tech industry and other places to just throw out these percentages, they’re not based on anything or calculated based on anything. [In retrospect, I realize the tweet was probably referencing the concept of P(doom), but I still think it’s silly.]
One thing I will say about Coxon’s statement and decision is — there’s this recurring theme on Equity, when someone like Sam Altman or Dario Amodei is doing this doomer narrative, there’s always this element of: Well, then, why are you doing what you’re doing? If you actually believe that [AI could destroy humanity], you would not continue doing this.
[Whereas] this is actually somebody putting his professional trajectory where his mouth is. He’s actually saying, “I believe this is really, really, really bad, and I don’t want to keep working on it.” And so, props for having the courage to do that, if nothing else.
Kirsten: Yeah, I put him in a separate camp than everyone else saying that and talking about the dangers.
I’m going to put my speculative hat on, because I want to ask both of you a question, which is: Is it possible that every single time we see the increasing number of blog posts about yet another incident in which one of their AI agents breaks through unintentionally, or they talk about how humanity is at risk, is this a weird way of flexing to show how far advanced their company’s AI model is?
I mean, that sounds very cynical, but it does achieve that purpose. Which is: If these AI models weren’t advanced and weren’t capable and weren’t breaking through, we wouldn’t have to worry about these things, right? It’s like a very weird way to brag about the capabilities of the models that you’ve created within your own company.
Anthony: I’ve definitely wondered about this. I don’t think it’s completely cynical, in the sense that I don’t think it’s all just a very conscious marketing ploy across the board. I think that when a lot of these people — whether the researchers or CEOs — talk about it, they do have real concern.
But of course, it does align with [their] business interests in a lot of ways, to say, “Wow, we’ve built the most deadly software that’s ever been made.” I don’t want to get too psychoanalytic here, but others have pointed out that there is this temptation on a personal level of: Of course, you want to believe that the thing you’re working on is the most important and most dangerous thing in the world.
Sean: The thing that sticks out in my mind when I think about that question is, there’s certainly an element that makes it seem like, “Okay, we’re doing this thing that’s so capable, and that’s good for us in some way, even if it looks bad in a lot of different lights.”
I think what’s different about some of these most recent examples is, it really gives you the feeling that these companies don’t have a handle on this stuff in certain ways, especially with the OpenAI stuff.
We keep seeing more and more reporting about other internal agents that have accessed different wikis on the web and are leaving messages for each other, and in a way that doesn’t seem like it’s being handled in a competent way from OpenAI. I would imagine there would be just a bit more polish on the story being told, if it was wholly about getting people to believe that, “Oh my gosh, they’ve made something so incredibly capable.”
The other thing that I think is really fascinating about this, in particular, [is] we’re what, a few weeks at most out from seeing Anthropic’s S-1 filing for its IPO, and just a couple more weeks or month or two away from a potential IPO.
And the idea that you’re going to come out and say these things in this clear language ahead of an IPO — I’m very interested in what that means for that process. How much of this kind of stuff had they already written into the S-1 and the risk factors inside that document? Are there junior lawyers right now who are going through and having to rewrite that entire section of the S-1 filing to say, “It’s a officially Anthropic’s position that there’s a more than 10% chance that we could develop something that would eradicate all of humanity and that would be materially bad for our business”?
Kirsten: You’re assuming that it’s not in there already.
Sean: That’s what I’m saying, though: Is it in there already and being reworded? Or is this something that’s a true scramble? There has to have been language in there. It’s one of the reasons I’m so eager to read this document in a way that goes even further, in some ways, than the SpaceX [S-1], because I’m sure that there’s probably stuff specific to these ideas that will be interesting to see.
Kirsten: Here’s the thing: In a traditional investment environment, one might believe that language like this would hurt the valuation of a company, because it’s suddenly dangerous. But we don’t live in normal times.
And so again, back to my point, it could end up being a weird beneficial flex for the company on the valuation side. It’s not the same as the whole rage-baiting trend that we saw last year, but it’s in that same, let’s say, universe, in which the strength, capability, even elements of danger of something, equals high valuation. So I guess we’ll see in a few weeks.
Putting that aside for a minute, what is being done about it? And can we control this? Tthe U.S. executive director of a nonprofit called ControlAI, Connor Leahy, he was on the show this week, talking about this. So what are you paying attention to in terms of how to control the dangerous aspects of AI, or are we throwing up our hands and watching it all unfold?
Anthony: I myself do not necessarily have a great answer to this, but I have been thinking about some aspects of this debate and maybe why I respond the way I do.
To echo one of Sean’s points, I do think that part of what this speaks to is the extent to which these major AI companies are feeling like they’re not really in control of these models anymore. That’s definitely not great. That is something that we should all be worried about.
I do think that part of the reason I’m skeptical of the doomer narrative or resistant to the doomer narrative is because it reaches this level of hysteria of, “Wow, this could destroy humanity in the next 10 years.” It is a little bit of a distraction from the more immediate harms that AI can have, whether that’s labor-related, whether that’s environment- and climate-related.
Ideally, I think we should be able to discuss all of these things, and have regulatory and other kinds of safeguards against all of these things [including AI’s existential threat]. But once you start using phrases like AGI and superintelligence, that just sucks up all the oxygen in the room in a way that is not very helpful.

articles.title: AI could make thinking cheap. What happens to jobs, education and human purpose?
articles.text:
AI could make thinking cheap. What happens to jobs, education and human purpose?
Dr. Pratosh, an IISc faculty member, warns that AI is not just coming for jobs—it could force a rethink of education, economics and what humans do for a living.
Artificial intelligence is no longer just beating us at chess or drafting emails. It’s forcing an uncomfortable question: what happens to human purpose when raw intellect becomes a mass-produced commodity?
During a recent classroom discussion, Dr. Pratosh, Assistant Professor in the Department of Electrical Communication Engineering at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, didn't mince words. He framed our current moment as a potential “civilisational crisis.”
“If intelligence is commoditised, if thinking is commoditised, then what meaning does our existence have?” he asked.
This isn't just theoretical for him. Dr. Pratosh admitted he’s already stopped hiring research assistants for certain tasks. Why bottleneck a project with human speed when AI agents can work on dozens of complex problems simultaneously?
The New "Digital Feudal Lords"
The immediate fear isn't just job loss—it's who collects the rent. While tech optimists promise a future of AI-driven abundance, real-world economics suggests otherwise. Greater productivity doesn't automatically mean shared prosperity. In a capitalist system, the rewards naturally concentrate in the hands of whoever owns the computer, the chips, and the algorithms.
Dr. Pratosh warned that without structural changes, we could easily land in a form of digital feudalism. For a country like India, with its massive workforce reliant on knowledge-intensive jobs, the economic fallout over the next few years could be profound.
Why Pay for a Degree When AI is the Best Teacher?
If AI can instantly write, code, analyse, and research, what is the point of standard university degrees?
Dr. Pratosh shared a telling personal account: his own daughter considers ChatGPT one of the best teachers she’s ever had. It never loses patience, never gets frustrated, and explains a concept ten different ways without judgment. If an AI can personalize education better than a standard classroom, universities can no longer sell information. They'll have to pivot to what AI can't offer: community, hands-on collaboration, and human connection.
Beyond the Benchmarks
“Enough of writing KL divergences; machines will figure that out,” Dr. Pratosh noted, urging students and educators to move past hyper-technical mechanical skills. Instead of teaching students to compete with AI, we need to teach them how to tackle real-world scientific and societal problems alongside it.
The real challenge ahead isn't building a smarter model. It's deciding what humans are actually for once thinking is no longer our exclusive domain.

articles.title: WhatsApp prueba la reproducción a doble velocidad para los estados en iPhone
articles.text:
WhatsApp prueba una función para reproducir a doble velocidad los videos de los estados en iPhone, una novedad que permitirá revisar publicaciones extensas en menos tiempo sin modificar ajustes permanentes. La herramienta aparece en la beta de WhatsApp para iOS y funciona mediante un gesto: mantener pulsado el lado derecho de la pantalla mientras se reproduce el contenido.
La opción importa porque llega después de que la aplicación ampliara hasta 30 segundos la duración de los clips musicales de los estados. Con más videos y publicaciones que se acumulan durante el día, la reproducción a 2x ofrece una vía rápida para consultar el contenido. Por ahora, solo algunos participantes de TestFlight pueden utilizar esta función en sus iPhone.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo será el mecanismo para adelantar la velocidad de los Estados
Para activar la velocidad, el usuario debe abrir un estado con video y mantener el dedo sobre el borde derecho del panel. La reproducción pasa de inmediato a 2x y conserva ese ritmo mientras exista contacto con la pantalla. Al retirar el dedo, el video recupera automáticamente su velocidad habitual. No hay un botón fijo ni una configuración adicional que habilitar.
El mecanismo replica una interacción que ya utilizan aplicaciones de video como Instagram, TikTok y YouTube. En lugar de introducir un menú específico, WhatsApp adopta un movimiento que buena parte de sus usuarios reconoce. La decisión reduce los pasos necesarios para acelerar una publicación y deja el control en manos de quien la visualiza. La velocidad normal vuelve sin interrupciones cuando finaliza la pulsación.
PUBLICIDAD
La novedad llega tras otro cambio reciente en los estados: WhatsApp permite ahora elegir la duración de los fragmentos musicales, con un máximo de 30 segundos. Antes, el límite era de 15 segundos y no existía la posibilidad de ajustarlo.
La ampliación da mayor margen para combinar imágenes, videos y canciones, aunque también aumenta el tiempo necesario para revisar una secuencia completa de actualizaciones. La reproducción acelerada busca compensar ese cambio en el consumo de contenido.
PUBLICIDAD
La prueba se limita por ahora a la beta de iOS
WABetaInfo detectó la función en la versión 26.36.10.70 de WhatsApp para iOS, distribuida mediante TestFlight. El despliegue no alcanza todavía a todos los probadores y tampoco tiene fecha confirmada para su llegada a la versión estable de la aplicación. Quienes no consigan activar el gesto deberán esperar a futuras actualizaciones. WhatsApp suele liberar estas herramientas de manera gradual para comprobar su funcionamiento antes de extenderlas.
Los estados son publicaciones temporales que desaparecen después de 24 horas y permiten compartir imágenes, texto, notas de voz y videos con los contactos. El formato se ha convertido en una herramienta habitual para mostrar momentos cotidianos, avisos o contenidos breves, aunque su consulta puede resultar extensa cuando hay muchas publicaciones consecutivas. La opción 2x responde a esa dinámica de uso y prioriza la rapidez.
PUBLICIDAD
La reproducción acelerada no altera el contenido original ni afecta a la publicación compartida por otra persona. Solo modifica de forma temporal la manera en que el usuario ve el video desde su propio dispositivo. Esta diferencia evita que la opción se confunda con una herramienta de edición o con un ajuste que quede guardado para futuras visualizaciones. También permite alternar entre ambas velocidades dentro del mismo estado, según el interés por una parte concreta.
La llegada de la reproducción a doble velocidad confirma que WhatsApp continúa ajustando los estados al consumo de video móvil. Por ahora, la prueba está restringida a una parte de los usuarios de iPhone inscritos en el programa beta. La empresa no ha comunicado cuándo ampliará la función al resto de dispositivos ni si llegará a Android.

articles.title: Apple Store : 3 gros changements arrivent dans les magasins Apple
articles.text:
Selon des informations obtenues de Bloomberg, les Apple Store du géant américain s’apprêtent à changer de visage. La marque semble souhaiter mettre en place un programme de rénovation de ses magasins dans les prochaines années. Apple réorganiserait ses espaces pour retrouver en efficacité et prendre en charge plus rapidement les clients.
1. Le grand retour des comptoirs en bois
Des Genius Bars entièrement conçus en bois feront leur réapparition dans de nombreux Apple Store. Ce nouveau mobilier reprendra l’esprit des comptoirs qui étaient présents à une époque tout en intégrant deux hauteurs de comptoir différentes pour faciliter l’accessibilité. Derrière ces zones de service, les murs intégreront des tiroirs de rangement ainsi que de grandes affiches dédiées à la présentation des nouveaux produits.
2. Au revoir les écrans géants
Les magasins se sépareront également des immenses écrans installés sur les murs au fond de la plupart des boutiques au cours des dernières années. Ces structures monumentales, qui servaient de décors pour les ateliers et le marketing, céderont définitivement leur place pour laisser le champ libre à l’implantation de nouveaux services.
À lire : Après le scandale Siri, Apple glisse un micro au Genius Bar
3. De nouveaux espaces dédiés au retrait et aux ateliers
Les sections situées sur les côtés des magasins, baptisées « Avenues », accueilleront deux types de baies en bois d’environ 3 mètres. Une première baie sera dédiée aux retraits de commandes en ligne, intégrant des tiroirs sécurisés et un logo discret sur sa partie supérieure avec une table pour gérer les remises de produits. Une seconde baie accueillera les ateliers, équipée d’un grand écran au-dessus, de rangements pour le matériel et de tabourets disposés autour d’une table fixe pour les vendeurs.

articles.title: La Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro est bradée à moins de 200 € maintenant que la GT 7 Pro est là — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le principe est connu : dès qu’un nouveau modèle débarque, l’ancien voit son prix fondre. C’est exactement ce qui arrive à la Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro, désormais éclipsée par la toute récente Huawei Watch GT 7 Pro. Sauf que la GT 6 Pro n’a rien perdu de ses arguments, avec tout un attirail de suivi sportif pensé pour le cyclisme, le golf ou la course. Bref, une montre haut de gamme qui vieillit très bien, et qui devient franchement intéressante à moins de 200 euros.
Les atouts de la Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro
- Boîtier en titane léger et résistant aux rayures
- Écran AMOLED de 466 x 466 pixels
- Suivi sportif avancé pour le cyclisme, le golf et la course
Affichée à 379,99 euros à sa sortie, la Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro version Black s’affiche désormais à 197,36 euros sur AliExpress une fois le code FWFR20 appliqué.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant la Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Un design en titane qui n’a pas pris une ride
Huawei ne réinvente pas la roue avec sa GT 6 Pro, et ça tombe bien. On retrouve ce format rond avec le rappel hexagonal sur le boîtier, devenu la signature des montres GT depuis deux ans. Comptez 45,6 x 45,6 x 11,25 mm pour 54 grammes sans le bracelet : c’est costaud sans être un poids lourd au poignet.
Les finitions restent le point fort de la maison. Boîtier en alliage de titane, dos en céramique et protection d’écran en verre saphir contre les rayures : on est clairement sur du haut de gamme. Le titane a le mérite d’être plus léger que l’acier tout en étant plus solide que l’aluminium. La GT 7 Pro reprend d’ailleurs cette même philosophie de matériaux, ce qui montre bien que la GT 6 Pro n’a pas grand-chose à lui envier sur ce terrain.
Le sport dans le viseur, avec quelques réserves
C’est là que la gamme GT justifie son nom : le suivi sportif. La Watch GT 6 Pro embarque des fonctions avancées pour le cyclisme, le golf et la course à pied, avec l’accéléromètre, la boussole électronique et l’analyse du sommeil de rigueur. Son écran AMOLED de 466 x 466 pixels reste lisible en plein effort, et la certification 5ATM plus les indices IP68 et IP69 permettent de la garder au poignet sous la pluie comme à la piscine.
Face à la GT 7 Pro, plus récente et forcément un cran au-dessus côté endurance, la GT 6 Pro reste amplement suffisante pour la grande majorité des sportifs, surtout à ce prix. Huawei annonce jusqu’à 21 jours, un chiffre théorique : en usage normal, comptez plutôt une douzaine de jours, et plusieurs dizaines d’heures dès qu’on sollicite le GPS en continu pour le sport. On reste très au-dessus des Apple Watch ou Galaxy Watch qu’on recharge quasiment tous les jours.
Pour creuser chaque critère technique, vous pouvez consulter notre test de la Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro, où l’on revient en détail sur ses fonctions sportives et son design.
Envie de la comparer à d’autres modèles avant de craquer ? Jetez un œil à notre guide des meilleures montres connectées du moment pour situer la Huawei face à la concurrence.

articles.title: WhatsApp sur iPad : une nouvelle interface avec barre latérale façon Mac est en déploiement
articles.text:
WhatsApp continue de faire évoluer son application pour iPad, quelques mois après avoir commencé à l’adapter au nouveau langage visuel d’Apple. Certains utilisateurs découvrent désormais une interface qui abandonne la barre de navigation inférieure au profit d’un panneau latéral inspiré de la version Mac.
L’application WhatsApp pour iPad n’a pas fini de changer. Après une première adaptation à Liquid Glass, la messagerie s’attaque cette fois à la manière dont ses différentes rubriques sont organisées à l’écran. Le changement est facile à repérer : la barre située en bas de l’interface disparaît et laisse place à une barre latérale. Un choix qui rapproche encore un peu plus l’expérience sur tablette de celle proposée sur Mac.
WhatsApp adopte une barre latérale inspirée du Mac
Avec cette nouvelle présentation, les principales rubriques de WhatsApp sont regroupées dans une barre verticale sur le côté de l’écran. On y retrouve les discussions, les actualités, les communautés et les appels, mais aussi Meta AI. L’ensemble reprend le principe déjà utilisé par WhatsApp sur Mac. Sur iPad, le panneau reste affiché à côté de la liste des conversations et de la discussion ouverte, sans empêcher l’utilisateur d’accéder au reste de l’interface.
Bonne nouvelle : il n'est toutefois pas obligatoire de le conserver à l’écran. WhatsApp permet en effet de masquer la barre latérale pour récupérer de l’espace. La liste des discussions et la conversation en cours peuvent alors s’étendre davantage vers le centre de l’écran.
La nouvelle interface de WhatsApp arrivera progressivement
Cette nouvelle organisation débarque quelques mois seulement après les premiers tests de Liquid Glass sur iPad. En juin dernier, WhatsApp avait commencé à proposer à certains bêta-testeurs des onglets, boutons et menus contextuels inspirés de la nouvelle interface d’Apple. La barre de navigation située en bas de l’écran était alors toujours présente.
D’après les découvertes de WABetaInfo, relayées par nos confrères de 9to5Mac, la barre latérale est actuellement proposée à certains utilisateurs de la dernière version disponible via TestFlight. Les bêta-testeurs ne sont d'ailleurs visiblement pas les seuls concernés. Des utilisateurs de la version classique distribuée sur l’App Store commencent eux aussi à voir apparaître cette nouvelle interface.
À l'heure où nous écrivons ces lignes, le déploiement n’est cela dit pas encore généralisé. Comme pour de nombreuses modifications de WhatsApp, l’arrivée de cette nouvelle présentation se fera progressivement auprès des utilisateurs.

articles.title: La Bataille de Gaulle : le succès continue avec la sortie SVOD et une grosse nouvelle pour la suite
articles.text:
Prochaine étape avant la course aux Oscars pour le film La Bataille de Gaulle : une sortie vidéo stratégique en DVD, Blu-ray, 4K et Steelbook dès le 4 novembre.
C’est l’un des braquages cinématographiques les plus spectaculaires de ces dernières années. En s’attaquant au mythe gaullien dans La Bataille de Gaulle, le réalisateur Antonin Baudry signe un diptyque historique dense (qu’on a adoré) et transforme un récit d’époque en thriller politique et militaire. Le film plonge le spectateur dans les coulisses de la débâcle de 1940, retraçant la trajectoire d’un général inconnu qui s’envole pour Londres, seul contre tous, avec l’ambition suicidaire d’entretenir la flamme de la Résistance.
Quand De Gaulle devient le rouleau compresseur des salles de cinéma
Porté par un bouche-à-oreille exceptionnel, ce projet titanesque en deux volets (L’Âge de fer et J’écris ton nom) s’est imposé comme le raz-de-marée cinématographique de l’année en France. Alors que L’Âge de fer passe le cap des 3 millions d’entrées et que le second volet le talonne à 2,58 millions, la fresque vise désormais la barre mythique des 6 millions de billets vendus. Une longévité rare en salles. Après quatorze semaines d’exploitation, L’Âge de fer figure parmi les cinq films présélectionnés par le CNC pour représenter la France aux Oscars 2027.
Loin du roman national trop lisse et des statues de bronze poussiéreuses, le réalisateur du Chant du loup s’attaque au mythe par le prisme de l’urgence absolue. Baudry retrace cette poignée de semaines où tout a failli basculer, lorsque des adolescents révoltés, des soldats perdus et des résistants de l’ombre ont rejoint cet officier isolé. Pour porter cette saga de plus de cinq heures, le cinéaste réunit un casting d’exception : Simon Abkarian, Niels Schneider, Anamaria Vartolomei, Benoît Magimel et Thierry Lhermitte.
Une édition physique taillée pour les collectionneurs
Pathé Films sort le grand jeu pour prolonger ce succès historique juste avant les fêtes de fin d’année. L’intégrale des deux volets sera disponible à la vente le 4 novembre 2026 comme on peut l’apprendre via un communiqué de presse Pathé:
- Éditions DVD et Blu-ray classiques : Proposées en bipack au tarif de 24,99 €
- Éditions Ultra HD 4K + Blu-ray & Steelbook : Proposées au tarif de 39,99 €
Une sortie événement pour replonger chez soi dans l’une des fresques les plus ambitieuses du cinéma français récent.

articles.title: Blizzard Confirms Diablo 5 Details, Players Share a "Unique Bond" With Diablo Himself
articles.text:
Monday, September 14th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Blizzard Confirms Diablo 5 Details, Players Share a "Unique Bond" With Diablo Himself
Diablo 5 is officially targeting a Spring 2029 release window, and the studio is now filling in story details about the world players will inhabit. Narrative director Jennifer Hepler explained that the protagonist shares what she called a "unique bond" with Diablo himself. "As you play, you find out how and why it came to be," she said, adding that this connection is what lets the character face the Lord of Terror while also leaving them vulnerable to his power. That link apparently opens the door to the Terror Realm, Diablo's personal domain, which players can enter and survive, something Hepler says unlocks unspecified new abilities the team isn't ready to detail yet.
The bigger structural change is that there are apparently no towns anymore. Since Diablo already won by the time the game starts, there are no functioning settlements left, so players build a traveling caravan instead, picking up merchants, craftspeople, and companions along the way. Blizzard is also introducing what it calls Terror Forming, where the world visibly changes each time players return to a location, courtesy of corrupting Dread Commanders reshaping the terrain. Three years is a long wait, but Blizzard will probably keep drip-feeding these updates before launch, which at least gives fans plenty to argue about in the meantime.

articles.title: Obama urges Democrats to have a ‘clear plan’ for AI safeguards | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Former President Barack Obama recently said that Democrats need to make artificial intelligence one of their “central agendas” and “have a very clear plan” to address concerns around the technology’s economic impact and safety, according to The New York Times.
Obama made these comments on Thursday, at Democratic fundraising event where he was interviewed by House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries. The NYT says that Obama’s office provided a partial transcript of the event, at which Jeffries asked Obama how congressional Democrats should approach AI.
In response, Obama said that once Democrats regain the House majority, they need to “put together a framework for a very public conversation.”
“This is something that is moving very fast in private hands, and if we don’t get on top of it, I think can be dangerous,” Obama added. “If we do get on top of it, I do think it’s beneficial. I genuinely think it’s going to accelerate, for example, drug development in ways that can help us cure diseases.”
In a statement, Jeffries said the former president “is correct that decisive action must be taken on artificial intelligence.” Jeffries also said that “Republicans have abdicated their responsibility to govern on behalf of the American people.”
The NYT also reports that Obama has offered himself as a “sounding board” to AI executives and has spoken to both Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. His comments come amidst growing concern around AI safety, particularly after an AI researcher resigned from Anthropic and claimed the leading AI companies are “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.”
On Saturday, Amodei outlined a broad approach to “pacing the frontier,” which would include giving independent safety evaluators access to leading AI companies and models, as well as developing “common safety standards” between companies. In social media posts, Altman and SpaceX CEO Musk seemed to respond positively to Amodei’s plan, with Altman saying that OpenAI would also commit to “having independent evaluators with employee-like access.”
President Donald Trump, meanwhile, discussed AI safety concerns with reporters at an Irish golf event on Sunday. Bloomberg reports that Trump boasted that the United States is “the most sophisticated country in the world,” adding that he wants “to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins.” (Earlier this year, the Trump administration released a legislative framework for AI that would preempt state laws and shift the child safety burden to parents.)
“And we can put guardrails,” Trump said. “We can do this and that. But I think you have a lot of negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn’t be bringing it up.”

articles.title: La nueva lavadora triple de Xiaomi es el sueño de cualquier hogar: soluciona el problema de lavar poca ropa
articles.text:
Sí, Xiaomi se ha sumado a la moda de las lavadoras triples. Desde hace varios meses, diferentes marcas del sector están lanzando este producto con una novedad bastante interesante: tambores extra en los que caben 1 o 2 kg de ropa para hacer lavados pequeños sin desperdiciar agua, energía o detergente. Pues bien, la marca china, como ya nos tiene acostumbrados, acaba de lanzar su propia versión para dejar al resto con la cara roja. Es barata, cuenta con funciones de IA impresionantes y todas las ventajas de esos tambores extra.
Su nombre es Xiaomi Mijia Triple-Tube Washing Machine y cuenta con una capacidad total de 14 kg de ropa. Su tambor principal puede lavar hasta 11 kg y los dos tambores pequeños hasta 1,5 kg cada uno. Y, por supuesto, son totalmente independientes: pueden funcionar los tres a la vez o por separado.
Todos tienen los mismos sistemas de lavado y están conectados al sistema de detergente y agua, por lo que poner una lavadora pequeña es tan fácil como meter la ropa en uno de los tambores mini e iniciar el programa que quieras.
Esto es ideal para lavar 2-3 camisetas, la ropa interior o prendas de color delicadas que necesiten un programa específico. Todo, sin tener que meterlo en el tambor grande y desperdiciar una gran cantidad de agua y detergente. Y, por si no queda claro, Xiaomi permite configurar un programa diferente en cada tambor.
Además, a pesar de tener tres tambores, su tamaño es bastante compacto: tiene el mismo ancho que una lavadora tradicional y solo es un poco más alta por motivos obvios.
No solo es una lavadora triple, Xiaomi ha metido toda su tecnología en el interior
Esta lavadora no solo es interesante por su configuración de triple tambor, sino que también incluye varias de las tecnologías más avanzadas de Xiaomi. Por ejemplo, cuenta con una desinfección completa del aparato con agua fría, por lo que no es necesario lavar con agua caliente para asegurarse de que los tambores permanezcan libres de bacterias.
Ahora bien, la joya de la corona es su IA. Xiaomi incluye un sistema de IA que detecta las prendas y te aconseja cómo lavarlas, además de un reconocimiento para que puedas describir el tipo de ropa, el color o el tejido con la voz y que ella configure el programa más adecuado para cada tambor.
Por supuesto, también incluye varios depósitos de detergente y suavizante para cargarlos con grandes cantidades y que este sea gestionado automáticamente en cada lavado dependiendo de la carga, el programa y el tambor seleccionado. Programas, por otro lado, que se pueden gestionar a distancia desde la app Mi Home para, por ejemplo, cargar la lavadora y programar el lavado para que termine justo cuando llegas a casa.
Ahora las malas noticias. Por mucho que te guste esta lavadora de Xiaomi, por ahora solo se puede pedir en China. Su precio es más que atractivo: cuesta menos de 600 euros al cambio. Si se lanzará en España es, por ahora, una completa incógnita.

articles.title: Kleiner als gedacht: Forscher machen in Aufnahmen des Merkur überraschende Entdeckungen
articles.text:
Merkur schrumpft schneller als gedacht: Warum der Planet einmal deutlich größer gewesen sein könnte
Merkur ist der kleinste Planet unseres Sonnensystems und gilt bisher als wenig erforscht. Wissenschaftler:innen des Deutschen Zentrums für Luft- und Raumfahrt haben jetzt untersucht, wie stark sich der Radius des Himmelskörpers im Laufe der Zeit aufgrund seiner Abkühlung verringert hat. Dabei machten sie eine interessante Entdeckung, die frühere Schätzungen infrage stellt.
Merkur könnte viel größer gewesen sein
Heute entspricht die Oberfläche des Merkur etwa der des Indischen Ozeans. Laut den Forscher:innen könnte der Planet bei seiner Entstehung allerdings deutlich größer gewesen sein. Zwar ist schon lange bekannt, dass Merkur beim Abkühlen geschrumpft ist. Das genaue Ausmaß dieser planetarischen Kontraktion könnte laut der neuen Studie aber tatsächlich um zehn bis 30 Prozent unterschätzt worden sein. Bei der Untersuchung aktualisierter Karten der Planetenoberfläche stellten die Wissenschaftler:innen fest, dass die durch die Kontraktion entstandenen felsigen Falten, sogenannte „Verkürzungsstrukturen”, nicht so gleichmäßig über das Gelände verteilt sind, wie es bisherige Modelle vorhersagen.
Das bedeutet, dass Merkur bei seiner Entstehung einen Radius gehabt haben könnte, der vier bis sechs Meilen größer war als heute – ein Unterschied von etwa sechseinhalb bis knapp zehn Kilometern. Das Forschungsteam erkannte, dass die chaotischen Ablagerungen, die bei Einschlägen auf dem Planeten zurückblieben, viele dieser Verkürzungsstrukturen verdecken. Das habe zu früheren Unterschätzungen der Schrumpfung geführt. „Unsere Korrektur hinsichtlich der radialen Kontraktion des Merkur liefert neue Einblicke in die thermische Entwicklung des Planeten”, so das Team unter der Leitung von Gaku Nishiyama in seiner Studie. Die Ergebnisse wurden in der Fachzeitschrift Geophysical Research Letters veröffentlicht.
Mission soll neue Erkenntnisse liefern
In naher Zukunft könnten noch weitere Erkenntnisse über den Merkur möglich werden. Die Mission „Bepicolombo“ brach schon im Jahr 2018 zu dem Planeten auf und hat ihn inzwischen erreicht. Wie die Europäische Weltraumorganisation Esa Anfang September in einer Pressemitteilung bekannt gab, koppelte sie im Rahmen eines äußerst komplexen Prozesses zwei Orbiter vom Raumfahrzeug ab. Diese sollen in den kommenden Jahren neue Daten über den Planeten sammeln. Der „Mercury Planetary Orbiter” (MPO) widmet sich der direkten Erkundung des Himmelskörpers und kartiert dessen Oberfläche präzise. Der zweite „Mercury Magnetosphere Orbiter“ (Mio) wird den Planeten in größerem Abstand umfliegen, um sein Magnetfeld zu untersuchen.
Seit dem Start der Mission hat das Raumfahrzeug eine Strecke von rund 207 Millionen Kilometern zurückgelegt. Auf seiner Reise passierte es den Merkur schon mehrere Male, um die optimale Flugbahn für das Absetzen der Orbiter einzunehmen. Nach dem geglückten Abtrennungsmanöver sollen die beiden wissenschaftlichen Sonden im November gemeinsam in die Umlaufbahn des Merkur eintreten. Für den Folgemonat ist die Trennung der beiden Orbiter voneinander vorgesehen, bevor der reguläre wissenschaftliche Messbetrieb im April 2027 beginnt. Bei der „Bepicolombo”-Mission arbeitet die Esa eng mit der japanischen Raumfahrtbehörde Jaxa zusammen.

articles.title: Wie Google KI-Agenten von schädlichem Verhalten auf deim Smartphone abhalten will
articles.text:
Sicherheitskäfig: Wie Google KI-Agenten davon abhalten will, Schaden auf deinem Smartphone anzurichten
Autonome KI-Agenten sollen künftig noch stärker als bisher eigenständig Aufgaben wie das Planen und Buchen von Reisen übernehmen. Damit sie dabei keinen Schaden auf dem Smartphone anrichten, hat Google Vorbereitungen getroffen und eine Art Sicherheitskäfig in sein mobiles Betriebssystem Android integriert.
Sicherheitskäfig für KI-Agenten in Android
Wie Android Police berichtet, handelt es sich dabei aber nicht um eine von den Nutzer:innen steuerbare Funktion. Hinweise auf die Schutzmaßnahme finden sich demnach bisher lediglich in Dokumenten von Entwickler:innen und in Release-Notes von Software Development Kits.
Zentraler Teil der Sicherheitsfunktion für KI-Agenten ist das Android-Framework Appfunctionsmanager. Darin ist ein Tool integriert, das für Systemberechtigungen zuständig ist. Jede App und jeder KI-Assistent benötigt die Erlaubnis des Execute-App-Functions genannten Systems, um eine Aktion vorzunehmen.
KI-Agenten über Shortcuts steuern
Künftig soll dieses Framework dazu dienen, Aktionen von KI-Agenten per Shortcut freizugeben. Dahinter steckt die Idee, dass KI-Agenten über bestimmte Shortcuts gesteuert werden, statt sich wie menschliche Nutzer:innen durch Website-Menüs und Button-Wirrwarr zu klicken. Das soll die Fehlerquote verringern. Kritische Aktionen wie das Löschen von Daten oder Bezahlvorgänge sollen derweil weiter die Freigabe der Nutzer:innen erfordern.
Android Police beschreibt die Shortcuts wie eine Art Hyperlink für spezielle Aufgaben. Als Beispiel dient die Aufforderung an einen Gemini-basierten KI-Agenten, eine Reise zu buchen. Bisher gibt es allerdings so gut wie keine entsprechenden Shortcuts.
Sicherheitssystem noch im Testmodus
Denn noch befindet sich das System im Testmodus. Lediglich ein kleines Team von Google-Entwickler:innen soll Zugriff darauf haben. Wann das Projekt das Tageslicht erblickt, ist noch unklar. Möglich ist auch, dass Google es noch komplett umkrempelt.
Noch schreitet die Gemini-Integration in Android ohnehin langsam voran. So soll Googles KI-Assistent in zehn hauseigene Apps integriert sein, von denen nur drei nützlich sein sollen. Der Zugang ist auch hier auf ausgewählte Entwickler:innen beschränkt.

articles.title: I was ready to give these cheap Soundpeats open earbuds a perfect review — but one recurring issue became their downfall
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
There's a lot to like about the Soundpeats Pop Clip2 open earbuds: they sound fantastic, fit comfortably, have loads of useful features and last a long time. Moreover, they're one of the most affordable examples of their 'ear-cuff' form factor. However, rampant connection problems — and even some charging issues — mean they're harder to recommend than worse-performing rivals.
Pros
- +Affordable price
- +Fantastic sound
- +Plenty of handy features
Cons
- -Rampant connectivity woes
- -Case breaking problems
- -Confusing dual name
Why you can trust TechRadar
Soundpeats Pop Clip2: Two-minute review
There's a version of this Soundpeats Pop Clip2 that you'll never read. After several weeks with the Soundpeats Clip1's cheaper successor, I was half-way through writing a five-star review which declared them the best open earbuds you could buy. That version is, as you can already tell, not this version of the review.
You see, the longer I used the Soundpeats Pop Clip2, the more I had to contend with some annoying issues; the kind of problem which often emerge after months or years of use, especially in cheaper tech, but shouldn't be affecting the buds after just a few weeks.
For example, I had an issue with the charging case, where it wouldn't reliably power up the buds. Sometimes I'd take them out, only to find them drained. My biggest problem, though, was with connectivity: they'd often fail to connect to my phone, or repeatedly drop out while I was running. A few times, when I needed some buds for a cycle or run, I'd just use the recently-reviewed Baseus Bowie MC2 rather than try and fight with the Pop Clip 2.
It's a shame, because aside from these common cheap-bud problems, the Soundpeats Pop Clip 2 are genuinely fantastic earbuds. Or is it the Soundpeats UU2? Depending on where you live, they're called one or the other, but in many countries the brand is using both names. Confusing. I’m going to be using the former name, because it simply makes more sense.
The Soundpeats Pop Clip2 have to be some of the best-sounding clip-style earbuds I’ve heard: they have a nice simple V-shaped sound, offering bass with ‘oomph’ but tone, and clear crisp treble. They don’t re-invent the wheel, but nimbly avoid all the issues that come with audio in buds of this form factor.
They tick loads of other boxes too: they last longer than most rivals, fit really well, and offer a solid list of features like spatial audio, sound leak prevention and water drainage.
Perhaps most importantly, Soundpeats has defied our price-hike current state of living by dropping the price of the Pop Clip2 (compared to the predecessor). And not by a few pennies either: $20 in the US, £15 in the UK, $9.99 in Australia (okay, that one’s not a dramatic drop). The brand already had some of the best value open-ears on the market, and it’s really pressing its advantage here.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
But because of the connection problems, they're a write-off, right? Uh, I'm not so sure. These problems were persistent, but not consistent. I frequently went for hours without a connection drop or problem, and found ways to cater for some of the quirks. As I write this mini-review, I've been seated at my desk and listening for three hours straight, without any problem. But I know if I went outdoors, they'd be less reliable.
I wish I could recommend the Soundpeats whole-heartedly, and the issues make that impossible. But it's possible that your mileage will vary, or that the brand will fix some of the connection issues through software patches.
Soundpeats Pop Clip2 review: Price and release date
- Launched in August 2026
- Sells for $49.99 / £59.99 / AU$70
- Cheaper than predecessors and other rivals
The Soundpeats Pop Clip2 were unveiled on August 10, 2026, just nine months after the unveiling of their predecessors, the Soundpeats Clip1. That’s not a long time to wait for them to… pop out.
At launch, the buds were tapped for a $49.99 / £59.99 / AU$70 asking price, which is cheaper than the $69.99 / £74.99 / AU$79.99 asking price of the last model. But just two weeks after release, I’m finding them available for £36 in the UK, so they may be even cheaper than reported. Let me be clear: this is rock-bottom prices territory from a trusted brand.
OK, they’re not technically the cheapest open earbuds around — there are options in the backrooms of Amazon and AliExpress that are much cheaper — but they’re the cheapest from a known, respected name in audio (notwithstanding sales on Soundcore, Baseus and Earfun products, which see them dip below Soundpeats’ cost).
The thing is, value only comes into effect if the performance is worth even the nominal outlay you'll have to part with to own them. So let's dig into that.
Soundpeats Pop Clip2 review: Specs
| Drivers | 12mm | 
| Active noise cancellation | No | 
| Battery life | 10 hours (buds), 42 hours (case) | 
| Weight | 5.1g (buds), 47.7g (case) | 
| Connectivity | Bluetooth 6.0 | 
| Frequency response | Not specified | 
| Waterproofing | IPX5 | 
Soundpeats Pop Clip2 review: Features
- Solid 10h/42h battery life
- App offers loads of features
- Connectivity problems plague experience
The Soundpeats Pop Clip2 offer a 10-hour battery life per bud, and in testing they lasted that long regularly. According to the brand, the case offers a total of up to 42 hours. Both of those sums are a little above average, and I'd say they're enough for most uses.
There's no ANC here, but the Soundpeats app offers basically every other feature under the sun. There's spatial audio, find my earbuds, a low-latency gaming mode, a privacy mode to reduce sound leakage, a drainage function to shake water droplets out if the buds get wet, a dynamic EQ tool which adjusts your sound on the fly, and of course an equalizer.
This latter lets you choose between a range of presets based on genre, though it turns off dynamic EQ and spatial audio. There's an adaptive and custom mode too, but for some reason, you can only use these if you create a free Soundpeats account. Locking an essential tool unless someone hands you their email? Thumbs down from me.
In the Soundpeats app, you can also toggle LDAC and set up multi-point connection, as well as change what the gesture controls do.
Now, it's time to get to the elephant in the room, the one I mentioned in the review introduction. I had a bad time with the Soundpeats Pop Clip2's connectivity (or lack thereof).
Frequently, I'd remove the buds from the case, only for one to fail to connect. I never figured out a solution to this issue, though sometimes holding the 'on' button kicked it into gear, and it often prompted me to just pick up a rival pair of buds which actually connected.
Even when the Clip2 did connect, I'd sometimes have to contend with drop outs or a stuttery connection, particularly on whichever of the buds was furthest from the phone. And I wasn't using the buds at the extreme of their connection range; my phone could literally be in one hand, and the bud on the other side of my face would keep dropping out.
So, despite the use of Bluetooth 6.0 (and, of course, my attempts to fix the problem by changing phones and updating the firmware), connection is a real issue here. Depending on the root cause, it could be fixable with a software patch, but it might be an intrinsic problem with the buds.
- Features score: 3.5/5
Soundpeats Pop Clip2 review: Design
- Few differences from predecessor
- Case is small, but with problems
- Earbuds fit reliably and comfortably
The big Soundpeats Pop Clip2 difference from its predecessor is the case, which is smaller and more convenient to tote around. It's a small pebble, weighing 47.7g, which fits in a pocket with no problem.
There is a problem, but it's inside. Like in some other cheap earbuds I've tested, the charging pins in the Clip2 case can often get stuck down. These are those shiny needles which touch the connectors on an earbud, in order to power it up while it's in the case, depressing as they do. In some cases, they can fail to spring back up, sometimes stopping working entirely.
I often managed to free the charging pins by pressing them down and wiggling, but often I only knew to do this when a bud had failed to charge. That is to say, there's a manual solution, but I would've preferred earbuds that just worked.
Charging issues aside, the buds work great, which is no surprise given that they're almost identical from the wonderful previous-generation Clips. they're light, at roughly 5g per unit, and you can easily forget you're wearing them.
The fit is solid, and I never found any issues with them shaking or falling out of place while I was on a run. When it comes to the Pop Clip2's actual earpieces, I have no notes.
This extends to the on-bud controls. Instead of relying on a large and vague tap control, Soundpeats has placed a physical button on each bud, which is easiest to press by pinching the body of the device. This is easy to trigger, even when you're active, and a satisfying 'click' lets you know your gesture has been accepted.
A note to buyers: head to the app and customize what single, double-, triple-tap and long-held functions do. I didn't love the default options, but luckily it's easy to change.
- Design score: 4/5
Soundpeats Pop Clip2 review: Sound quality
- These are the best open earbuds I've heard
- Lovely balanced sound with plenty of customization
- 12mm drivers, LDAC and Hi-Res Audio Wireless
Several open earbuds makers have experimented with different multi-driver set-ups in order to solve the core problem with the form factor – getting good sound is incredibly tricky when the bud is far from your ear – and yet somehow Soundpeats has made the biggest leaps with a single driver.
Put simply, the Pop Clip 2 are the best-sounding open earbuds I’ve used to date, a compliment that’s a little limited in its reach but no less earnest for it. Each bud has a 12mm dual-magnetic driver, which according to Soundpeats has been tuned for “deep bass”, and seems on paper at least to match the Clip1’s driver. In practice, though, it performs a lot better.
By default, the earbuds have a fairly neutral sound profile, not favoring bass, mids or treble too heavily, and that’s pretty rare for exercise buds. In Handle With Care by Traveling Wilburys, I was surprised to hear the various rhythmic and harmonic instruments alongside the vocals and bass, and in Cinnamon by The Long Winters, it was easy to pick out the various simultaneous guitar lines which, in worse earbuds, blur together.
Despite this neutral focus, treble and bass are both handled well: the latter is bright, clear and crisp, the latter well-defined and energetic. And, thankfully, my Clip1 gripe about the max volume being too low has been fixed.
The buds’ sound can be pulled six ways from Sunday if you’ll let them too. In the dynamic mode, the bass and treble were boosted for a lovely V-shaped audio which gave Two Door Cinema Club’s Sleep Alone a lovely, bouncing energy.
Contributing to the sound is the Bluetooth codec support which Soundpeats has added — at least the connection works in one way. The buds support LDAC, and are certified for Hi-Res Audio Wireless, which isn’t something you can say about every set of open earbuds.
Of course, much of your enjoyment will depend on how you listen. No matter how good open-ears sound in the comfort of your home, the sound quality will plummet when you step outdoors into the busy word. But that’s the nature of the beast with these buds, and the dynamic equalizer went further than most in balancing for these issues.
- Sound quality: 5/5
Soundpeats Pop Clip2 review: Value
- Should be top-value earbuds
- Unfortunately, longevity isn't guaranteed
The Soundpeats Pop Clip2 sound fantastic and offer a solid range of features, despite being some of the cheapest open earbuds worth buying. They should be five-star buys.
Unfortunately, that appraisal would be forgetting the connection and case issues, two problems which sadly aren't uncommon in low-cost earbuds.
With that in mind, you're basically getting what you pay for, matching the promise of other same-price rivals: these are buds which work very well, but may stop working well before their time.
- Value: 3.5/5
Should I buy the Soundpeats Pop Clip2?
| Soundpeats Pop Clip2 score card |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Features | The feature set is impressive, but consistent connection problems make using the buds a drag. | 3.5/5 | 
| Design | The buds are smartly-designed and fit reliably and comfortably. Unfortunately, the case has a flaw. | 4/5 | 
| Sound quality | They're the best open-ear buds I've ever tested (admittedly, of a limited pool). | 5/5 | 
| Value | It's a fantastic package, but the various problems suggest a short lifespan. | 3.5/5 | 
Buy them if…
You need good-sounding open-ears
Most don't buy this form factor for the sound quality, but if you want something great-sounding, the Clip2 are second to none.
You want open-ears which fit reliably
Not once during many weeks of testing did the Clip2 ever fall out of my ears or ache during a workout.
You're on a budget
Don't buy super-cheap options for pennies. This is the cheapest option you should consider.
Don’t buy them if…
You need something reliable
My Clip2 worked well when I found my way around their flaws. If you want something that works perfectly without having to put in the work, just skip these.
You want something that sounds good, full stop.
Just because these are the best-sounding open earbuds, doesn't mean they're fantastic in the grand scheme of things. If you want workout headphones with fantastic sound, you need something with an in-ear seal, or over-ears.
Soundpeats Pop Clip2 review: Also consider
Looking for other affordable clip-style earbuds? Here are a few we've tested and would recommend.
| Header Cell - Column 0 | Soundpeats Pop Clip2 | Baseus Bowie MC2 | Anker Soundcore AeroClip | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Drivers | 12mm | 11mm | 12mm | 
| Active noise cancellation | No | No | No | 
| Battery life (ANC on) | 10 hours (buds), 42 hours (case) | 11.5 hours (buds), 55 hours (case) | 8 hours (buds), 24 hours (case) | 
| Weight | 5g (buds), 47.7g (case) | 5.1g (buds), 51g (case) | 6g (buds), 42g (case) | 
| Connectivity | Bluetooth 6.0 | Bluetooth 6.0 | Bluetooth 5.4 | 
| Waterproofing | IPX5 | IP67 | IPX4 | 
Baseus Bowie MC2
The buds I tested before the Clip2, which I kept cheating on the Soundpeats with, don't sound as good or have the same feature set. But they're more reliable and last for longer between charges.
Read our full Baseus Bowie MC2 review
Anker Soundcore AeroClip
These earbuds have decreased in price since they were released, so they now rival the Soundpeats. They sound great and have an app that is chock-full of features, even if other specs aren't as impressive.
Read our full Anker Soundcore AeroClip review
How I tested the Soundpeats Pop Clip2
- Tested for roughly four weeks
- Paired with two different Android phones for music, podcasts, movies and games
- Used on runs, at gym, at desk and during travels
To write this full review, I used the Soundpeats Pop Clip2 for the best part of one month. In that time, I used it paired to two different Android smartphones: the Fairphone 6 Plus and Samsung Galaxy Z Fold.
To test the earbuds, I used them for various fitness activities including walks, runs, cycles and trips to the gym. I also used them while working at my desk, on the train and on a flight. Mostly, my listening was done on Spotify, but I also used Tidal and several video streaming services, played games and conducted calls with them.
I've been reviewing for TechRadar since early 2019, and over the last few years, that's included plenty of open earbuds, including the stablemates of the product here, the Soundpeats Clip1. I've also used various other Soundpeats headphones and earbuds.

articles.title: Windows 11 : la mise à jour de septembre peut casser le son de votre PC
articles.text:
C’est désormais une (mauvaise) habitude. À chaque déploiement d’une mise à jour, Windows 11 est touché par de nouveaux bugs. Après avoir installé le dernier Patch Tuesday déployé la semaine dernière par Microsoft, de nombreux utilisateurs ont pu s’en apercevoir.
Car si la mise à jour de septembre corrige près de 1000 failles de sécurité et introduit d’importantes nouveautés dans Windows 11, elle est aussi à l’origine d’un nouveau bug aussi vilain que problématique.
Après l’avoir installé, de nombreux utilisateurs rapportent que leur PC est incapable de jouer le moindre son. Autre problème, et pas des moindres, chez certains utilisateurs, la mise à jour entraîne des plantages de l’Explorateur de fichiers. Des problèmes que Microsoft vient de confirmer dans une note publiée sur ses pages de support.
Des problèmes de son et de microphone
Le premier gros souci causé par l’installation de la mise à jour KB5124008 concerne la gestion du son. Chez certains utilisateurs, la mise à jour empêche en effet certains périphériques audio de démarrer ou d’émettre du son immédiatement après le redémarrage du PC.
Augmenter ou diminuer le volume sonore n’y changerait d’ailleurs rien, le système d’exploitation étant incapable d’initialiser le matériel. Le problème se produirait plus particulièrement sur les appareils utilisant la norme USB Audio Class 1.0.
La mise à jour est également à l’origine d’un autre souci. Elle entraîne un dysfonctionnement du microphone sur certains appareils ainsi que sur les machines disposant d’une configuration audio multicanal. Les micros perdent soudainement le son à cause d’un problème de détection de la configuration par Windows.
La page des paramètres de son de Windows peut chez certains utilisateurs, devenir totalement non réactive. Par ailleurs, une erreur affichant le message « Ce périphérique ne peut pas démarrer (code 10) » s’affiche dans le Gestionnaire de périphériques de Windows et la désinstallation ou la désactivation du périphérique ne permet pas de résoudre le problème.
En attendant qu’un correctif soit mis en ligne, Microsoft suggère de basculer l’appareil en mode 2 canaux sur les machines utilisant des équipements multicanaux. À noter que ce problème de son ne touche ni les casques ni les enceintes audio sans fil.

Source : Windows Latest

articles.title: "Ya estamos aburridos": un pueblo de Zamora se queda sin agua por unas vacas. Lo peor es que ya tenían problemas de abastecimiento
articles.text:
La semana pasada, San Román de Sanabria, un pequeño núcleo de la comarca de Cobreros (Zamora), se despertó sin una sola gota de agua en los grifos. Nadie había avisado de avería ni cortado el suministro, así que el pueblo empezó a preocuparse. Las culpables llevaban meses paseándose libremente por sus calles: unas vacas.
Buenos días, no hay agua. Por la noche, el depósito se fue vaciando sin que nadie se enterara. Los animales sueltos llegaron hasta una tubería enterrada a poca profundidad en una finca privada, la pisaron y la reventaron. El agua corrió durante horas, en plena noche, hasta agotar la reserva de todo el pueblo. La avería ya está reparada y el suministro ha vuelto, pero los vecinos ya están “aburridos” de esta situación.
Porque no es la primera vez que alguien se cruza con una en plena calle. Los vecinos lo llevan denunciando desde hace meses: ganado suelto campando por el casco urbano y por las carreteras cercanas, con el riesgo añadido de un posible atropello. La Guardia Civil tiene constancia.
Casi más vacas sueltas que vecinos. Galende, el municipio al que pertenece San Román, apenas suma 1.019 habitantes, repartidos entre el núcleo y pedanías como San Román, Cubelo o San Martín de Castañeda. La ganadería que campa a sus anchas por esas mismas calles es, con toda probabilidad, de raza Alistana-Sanabresa, la autóctona de esta comarca, criada en régimen extensivo por las sierras de Sanabria, Carballeda, Tábara, Alba, Guareña y Sayago.
Es irónico que la raza estuviera al borde de la extinción —de 35.000 cabezas en 1950 a solo 3.108 en todo el país en 2016— y hoy remonta con fuerza, un 8-10% de crecimiento anual, hasta un censo actual de unas 2.500 madres repartidas entre 39 ganaderos de la provincia. Este modelo de cría, vaca libre por el monte, ha sido esencial para su recuperación.
No es solo San Román. El mismo ganado suelto afecta también a Sotillo y Limianos, dos pueblos vecinos dentro de la misma red de núcleos de Cobreros. El alcalde, Luis Miguel López, ha trasladado el caso a la Sección Agraria Comarcal de Puebla de Sanabria y pide ya la intervención directa de la Junta de Castilla y León. El Ayuntamiento, por su parte, asegura haber agotado sus competencias para impedir que los animales entren en el pueblo.
En Riofrío del Órbigo, en León, los vecinos llevan más de un año conviviendo con un rebaño de unas 30 vacas sueltas por huertos, fincas y carreteras, sin que ni el Seprona ni la administración muevan ficha. "Parece que hasta que ocurra una desgracia nadie va a mover ficha", apuntan los afectados.
Disparos al aire y al cuerpo. En mayo de este año, en Morales del Vino, también en Zamora, una res brava se escapó de su explotación, hirió a un cuidador y amenazó con colarse en la A-66. La Guardia Civil tuvo que abatirla a tiros tras varias horas de operativo y dos dardos anestésicos que no surtieron efecto.
El Procurador del Común de Castilla y León tiene en su historial una queja formal de otra localidad zamorana, años atrás, por vacas sueltas que deambulaban por el casco urbano y contaminaban los manantiales del pueblo. La administración alegó falta de personal para abrir expediente sancionador.
Derrames y derramas. El agua es la gran cuestión. Zamora arrastra desde hace años una infraestructura hídrica al límite. La Diputación tiene en marcha un Plan Sequía que ha financiado obras de mejora del abastecimiento en 31 pueblos por más de 3,1 millones de euros. La Mancomunidad de Sayagua, pensada en 2010 para abastecer a 46 municipios con agua de mejor calidad, se convirtió en un fracaso: solo 9 de los 36 pueblos había resuelto el problema.
El 25 de febrero de 2026, la Diputación de Zamora aprobó una Convocatoria de Renovación de Redes de Abastecimiento con 2 millones de euros para sustituir tuberías de fibrocemento, ampliable hasta 2,6 millones y con capacidad para 80-100 obras. De hecho, en mayo se firmaron convenios con 51 ayuntamientos por 4,7 millones en obras excepcionales.
Tras lluvias persistentes del pasado marzo, detectaron turbidez en el agua de Fermoselle, Villalcampo, Palacios del Pan y San Pedro de la Nave-Almendra. Entonces pactaron con Iberdrola modernizar sus potabilizadoras (90% Diputación, 10% ayuntamientos), con solo el diagnóstico de Fermoselle cerrado en esa fecha (60.000 euros). El 13 de mayo firmaron un nuevo Plan de Emergencia de Abastecimiento de Agua por más de 950.000 euros para más de veinte municipios. Y el 12 de junio el Pleno amplió la convocatoria con 600.000 euros adicionales, hasta 2,6 millones, para cubrir las 108 solicitudes recibidas frente a las 84 que cubría la dotación inicial.
A día de hoy, todavía siguen faltando dotaciones, pero se han logrado grandes avances. Entretanto, Luis Miguel López, alcalde de San Román, considera necesaria la intervención de la Junta de Castilla y León para solucionar el drama de las vacas. Mientras no se diga lo contrario, ellas seguirán campando a sus anchas.

articles.title: The snake that cannot shed its skin must perish and fade
articles.text:
The snake that cannot shed its skin must perish and fade
Discover why personal growth requires change, adaptation, and renewal through the powerful lesson behind a snake shedding its skin.
“The snake which cannot cast its skin has to die.” This striking quote captures one of life's most important truths: growth demands change. A snake survives by shedding its old skin, making room for a new one. If it refuses or becomes unable to do so, its growth is restricted, and its survival is threatened. The same principle applies to human life. We cannot continue growing if we cling endlessly to outdated beliefs, unhealthy habits, past failures, or versions of ourselves that no longer fit who we are becoming.
Yet change is often uncomfortable. It requires us to leave behind what feels familiar and step into uncertainty. Many people resist transformation because it feels risky. However, just as the snake must shed its skin to live, individuals must embrace change to continue evolving. The quote reminds us that stagnation can be more dangerous than transformation.
Why change is essential for growth
Growth is impossible without change. Every stage of life brings new experiences, responsibilities, and lessons that shape who we are. The person you were five years ago is not the same person you are today because life has continuously transformed you.
When people refuse to adapt, they risk becoming trapped in old patterns. Growth requires learning new skills, developing new perspectives, and letting go of limitations that no longer serve a purpose. Change is not merely an option for improvement—it is a necessity for progress.
Holding on to the past can prevent progress
Many people struggle because they remain attached to old versions of themselves. Past mistakes, disappointments, fears, and regrets can become emotional burdens that hinder personal development.
Just as a snake cannot continue growing while trapped inside an old skin, people cannot reach their potential while clinging to outdated identities. Letting go of the past does not erase experiences; it allows individuals to learn from them and move forward with greater wisdom.
Transformation often feels uncomfortable
Shedding old skin is not an effortless process for a snake, and personal transformation is rarely easy for human beings. Change often brings uncertainty, challenges, and moments of self-doubt.
Starting a new career, ending an unhealthy relationship, pursuing a dream, or changing long-held beliefs can feel intimidating. However, discomfort is often a sign that growth is taking place. The most meaningful transformations frequently occur when people step beyond what feels safe and familiar.
The danger of stagnation
Remaining unchanged may seem comfortable, but stagnation carries its own risks. When people stop learning, adapting, and evolving, they can become disconnected from opportunities and personal fulfilment.
A stagnant life often leads to frustration because deep down, human beings are designed to grow. Refusing change may provide temporary comfort, but it can ultimately limit potential and prevent meaningful progress.
Shedding unhealthy habits
One of the most important forms of personal transformation involves letting go of harmful habits. Negative thinking, procrastination, fear of failure, and self-doubt can become like old skin that restricts growth.
Replacing these habits with healthier behaviours requires effort and persistence. However, every positive change creates space for new possibilities and personal development. Growth begins when individuals are willing to release what no longer benefits them.
Adapting to life's changing seasons
Life is constantly changing. Relationships evolve, careers shift, priorities change, and circumstances transform. Those who learn to adapt are often better equipped to navigate challenges and seize opportunities.
Adaptability does not mean abandoning values or identity. Instead, it means remaining open to learning and adjusting when necessary. Like the snake that sheds its skin, adaptable individuals understand that renewal is essential for survival and success.
Reinvention is a sign of strength
Some people view changing direction as a sign of inconsistency, but it is often a sign of courage. Reinvention requires self-awareness and the willingness to grow beyond previous limitations.
Many successful individuals have reinvented themselves multiple times throughout their lives. They recognized when old approaches no longer worked and embraced new ways of thinking and acting. Their success came not from remaining the same but from continually evolving.
The wisdom behind letting go
Letting go is not about losing something valuable; it is about creating space for something better. Every stage of growth requires releasing something from the past. Whether it is a limiting belief, a fear, or an outdated goal, letting go allows transformation to occur.
The wisdom of the quote lies in understanding that renewal is not a threat—it is a requirement for growth. What we release often makes room for what we are meant to become.
Why does that matter
“The snake which cannot cast its skin has to die” is a powerful metaphor for personal growth and transformation. Life demands renewal, adaptation, and the courage to let go of what no longer serves us. Just as a snake survives by shedding its old skin, people thrive by embracing change and welcoming new possibilities.
Growth is rarely comfortable, but it is always necessary. When we release outdated habits, limiting beliefs, and fears of the unknown, we create the opportunity to become stronger, wiser, and more capable versions of ourselves. In the end, transformation is not merely a part of life—it is the path to becoming who we are meant to be.

articles.title: Control Resonant : Remedy dévoile la configuration requise pour en prendre plein les yeux... et ça fait mal
articles.text:
Remedy revient à la charge en ce mois de septembre pour dévoiler plus en détail les configurations recommandées pour Control Resonant. Gourmand, très gourmand même, le titre nécessitera une bonne grosse machine pour tourner convenablement en 4K, en particulier si vous voulez du Path Tracing.
On sait depuis juin qu’une vieille GTX 1070 permettra de faire tourner tant bien que mal Control Resonant en 1080p / 30 FPS. Cette semaine, Remedy nous en dit plus sur les configurations recommandées pour lancer le jeu avec les meilleurs réglages disponibles sur PC… Et sans surprise, il faudra être rudement bien équipé pour le faire.
Une RTX 5080 au minimum pour la 4K avec Path Tracing
Dans leur version finale, les recommandations de Remedy stipulent donc une nouvelle fois que les GeForce GTX 1070, Radeon RX 5600 XT et Intel Arc A580 permettront de faire tourner le jeu en qualité basse, avec une définition Full HD et un framerate à 30 images par seconde.
Attention par contre, une RTX 2060 ou Radeon RX 6600 sont toutefois évoquées pour l’activation du ray-tracing avec les mêmes réglages. Et pour atteindre les 1440p / 60 FPS, sans ray-tracing, avec un upscaling équilibré, le studio finlandais préconise alors les RTX 3060 Ti, RX 6700 XT ou Arc B580.
Les choses sérieuses commencent lorsqu’on veut activer le ray-tracing en 1440p sans perdre le cap des 60 FPS. Pour ce faire, Remedy recommande cette fois une RTX 4070 Ti ou une Radeon RX 9070, tandis qu’une RTX 5080 est demandée, sans alternative chez AMD, pour tenir cette fois les 60 FPS en Ultra HD, avec du Path Tracing. À noter que, dans ce cas de figure, le studio mise sur de l’upscaling en mode performance… Ce qui signifie qu’on passera loin de la 4K native, en dépit de cette configuration déjà très musclée.
DLSS 4.5 et FSR 4.1 au menu pour soulager votre PC
Voici donc les principaux éléments à garder en tête :
Sans Ray Tracing
- Minimum (1080p, 30 FPS) : Carte graphique NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 / AMD Radeon RX 5600 XT / Intel Arc A580, 6 Go de mémoire vidéo, processeur Intel Core i5-8500 / AMD Ryzen 5 3500
- Recommandé (1440p, 60 FPS) : RTX 3060 Ti / RX 6700 XT / Arc B580, 8 Go de VRAM, i7-10700 / Ryzen 7 3700X
- Enthousiaste (2160p, 60 FPS) : RTX 3080 / RX 6800 XT, 10 Go de VRAM, i7-10700 / Ryzen 7 3700X
Avec Ray Tracing / Path Tracing
- RT Minimum (1080p, 30 FPS) : Carte graphique NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 SUPER / AMD Radon RX 6600 / Intel Arc A580, 8 Go de mémoire vidéo, Processeur Intel Core i7-8700K / AMD Ryzen 5 3600X
- RT Recommandé (1440p, 60 FPS) : RTX 4070 Ti / RX 9070, 10 Go de VRAM, i7-10700 / Ryzen 7 3700X
- Path Tracing Enthousiaste (2160p, 60 FPS) : RTX 5080 uniquement, 12 Go de VRAM, i7-10700 / Ryzen 7 3700X
Remedy recommande dans tous les cas un grand minimum de 16 Go de mémoire vive et des CPUs allant d’un modeste Core i5-8500 (ou AMD Ryzen 5 3500) pour jouer avec les réglages minimum, à un Core i7-10700 (ou AMD Ryzen 7 3700X) pour jouer avec le preset Path Tracing Enthusiast. On apprend enfin que la version PC du titre tirera profit du DLSS 4.5 de NVIDIA, mais aussi du FSR 4.1 d’AMD, avec Frame Generation dans les deux cas, pour permettre de soulager des PC déjà rudement mis à l'’épreuve.
Control Resonant est attendu sur PC, PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series S | X le 24 septembre prochain. Le titre sera par ailleurs proposé en bundle avec certaines cartes graphiques GeForce RTX dans le cadre d’un partenariat conclu entre Remedy et NVIDIA.
Source : VideoCardz / Remedy

articles.title: Remboursement du passe Navigo : jusqu'à 90,80 € dédommagés, la plateforme ouvre le 15 septembre
articles.text:
Si vous empruntez régulièrement les transports en commun franciliens, vous êtes peut-être éligibles à une campagne de remboursement. À la mi-septembre 2026, de nombreux usagers vont pouvoir demander un dédommagement pour les perturbations rencontrées sur certaines lignes du réseau.
Voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir sur cette nouvelle campagne de remboursement.
À partir de quand et où peut-on demander le remboursement ?
La campagne de remboursement débute le 15 septembre 2026. Toute la procédure se fait en ligne, sur la plateforme de dédommagement d’Île-de-France Mobilités. Elle n’est pas encore ouverte. Vous devriez cependant pouvoir y accéder depuis votre compte Île-de-France Mobilités Connect.
Qui est éligible au remboursement ?
Pour obtenir le remboursement, vous devez être abonné à un forfait Navigo. Il faut aussi avoir voyagé sur les lignes concernées, à la période où sont survenus les problèmes sur ces lignes.
Les justificatifs à fournir ne sont pas encore précisés, mais vous pouvez probablement déjà préparer le numéro de votre carte Navigo, un justificatif de domicile et une preuve de votre abonnement sur la période. Autant d’éléments qui devraient servir à prouver que vous avez bien emprunté régulièrement ces lignes et donc subi les désagréments.
Les lignes et les gares concernées en Île-de-France
Le dédommagement concerne les voyageurs qui ont emprunté :
- La ligne J,
- Et la ligne L.
Les trains de ces lignes ont subi d’importantes perturbations entre fin mars et mi-juillet 2026, « liées à l’immobilisation d’une partie du matériel roulant, à la suite d’un défaut sur le rail ayant abimé les roues de certains trains », indique un communiqué d’Île-de-France Mobilités. Par conséquent des trains ont été supprimés à plusieurs reprises, pendant plusieurs semaines.
La tempête survenue fin juin a également « entraîné une interruption totale de circulation entre Poissy et Les Mureaux du 28 juin au 5 juillet, impactant fortement l’ensemble de la ligne J ».
De quel montant pouvez-vous être remboursés ?
Le montant du dédommagement dépend de la ligne que vous avez l’habitude d’emprunter.
- Ligne J : équivalent d’un mois de forfait Navigo, soit 90,80 €.
- Ligne L : équivalent d’un demi-mois de forfait Navigo, soit 45,40 €.
Attention, certaines gares ne sont pas concernées
Si vous avez circulé sur ces axes, notez que certaines gares ne vous permettent cependant pas d’être éligibles au remboursement : Paris Saint-Lazare, Pont-Cardinet et La Défense.
« Ces gares ne sont pas concernées, étant desservies par plusieurs lignes du réseau », explique Île-de-France Mobilités.
